publication_note: This is a PUBLICATION-SAFE, metadata-only derivative of evaluation/m11d/holdout_annotations.json. The 'text' field of every claim has been redacted (set to null) because it is a verbatim or near-verbatim excerpt of a third-party employer's job-posting text, and this repository has not confirmed republication rights for that content. 'text_length_chars' and 'text_sha256' are preserved so a holder of the original (unpublished, local-only) annotation file can verify byte-for-byte that this metadata file was derived from the exact same frozen claims, without this public file itself reproducing any employer's copyrighted posting text. Every other field -- category labels, qualification_kind, necessity, logical_composition, github_observability, new_vocabulary_gap flags, domain/posting linkage -- is this project's own original analysis and is unaffected by the redaction.
annotation_methodology: Each claim below was independently annotated from the posting's own raw text (evaluation/m11d/source/*.txt, hash-frozen in provenance.json) BEFORE extract_competency_qualifications() or parse_job_description() was ever run against this corpus. Annotation did not inspect, anticipate, or back-fill from any extractor output. Ambiguity is preserved explicitly (necessity/applicability/github_observability may be marked uncertain in notes) rather than resolved to make a metric look better. New competency areas not present in M11-C's 17-tag vocabulary are marked new_vocabulary_gap=true -- these are the generalization-coverage findings this milestone exists to measure.
schema_notes: Mirrors evaluation/m11c/competency_extraction_controls.json's own field shape for direct comparability: text_category, is_applicant_qualification, qualification_kind, necessity, competency_concept, logical_composition, applicability_condition, github_observability, expected_conservative_projection.
